block.name: Slot Timing Monitor (CC)
block.doc:
Slot timing monitor for 5G-like burst experiments.
This block:
- Takes a complex baseband stream at the receiver side. - Passes it to the output unchanged (pass-through). - Reads the first rx_time tag from the UHD USRP Source in order to anchor the sample index to an absolute UHD time. - Detects burst starts by looking for rising edges of |x[n]|^2 above a configurable power threshold. - For each detected burst start, it: 1) computes the absolute burst time t_burst (seconds), 2) estimates the burst index k as the nearest integer to: k ≈ (t_burst - t0) / period_s, 3) computes the ideal burst time: T_tx(k) = t0 + k * period_s, 4) computes the timing error: D_k = t_burst - T_tx(k), 5) keeps a sliding window of recent D_k values and estimates jitter as the standard deviation of D_k.
The block prints one log line per detected burst:
[slot_timing_monitor_cc] burst k=K t_burst=... dt=... jitter=... (N=...)
It also exposes two accessors (for use from external C++/Python code):
- last_offset_s() : last timing error D_k in seconds. - last_jitter_s() : estimated jitter (seconds) over the current window.
Parameters:
- Sample rate (Hz) [samp_rate]: Sampling rate of the complex stream. Must match the UHD source (e.g. 30.72e6 for 5G-like numerology).
- First burst time t0 (s) [t0]: Expected absolute UHD time of the first transmitted burst. This should match the tx_time used at the transmitter for the first burst, e.g.: tx_time = {T0_integer, T0_fraction} then: t0 = T0_integer + T0_fraction.
- Burst period (s) [period_s]: Time between bursts. For example: 10 ms burst + 5 ms gap => period_s = 0.015 10 ms burst every 10 ms => period_s = 0.010
- Power threshold [threshold]: Threshold applied to |x[n]|^2. When the power crosses from below to above this value, a new burst start is detected. Choose a value above noise level and below your burst power.
- D(k) window length [dt_window_len]: Number of recent timing error samples D_k kept in a sliding window for jitter estimation. Larger window = smoother jitter but slower reaction.
Runtime configuration:
All parameters can be modified at runtime from GNU Radio Companion via callbacks (see below).
Usage in a 5G-like SDR experiment:
1) On the transmitter: - Schedule bursts using tx_time with a fixed grid: T_tx(k) = t0 + k * period_s for k = 0, 1, 2, ... - Use 10 ms bursts and 5 ms of silence if you want to emulate frame-based spectral sensing.
2) On the receiver: - Use UHD: USRP Source and connect it to this block. - Ensure that both TX and RX share the same UHD time domain (same 10 MHz and PPS if using multiple USRPs). - Place this block early in the RX chain, so that the power threshold still sees a clear burst structure.
3) Monitor the log outputs and the last_offset_s()/last_jitter_s() values to evaluate: - how stable the burst-to-burst timing is, - the mean offset between RX bursts and the ideal grid, - the timing jitter across bursts.
This block is intended as an analysis tool to verify that a USRP-based 5G-like burst transmission is correctly aligned in time at the receiver, using the same UHD time reference as tx_time and rx_time.
